answer: Each agent may submit only one claim per epoch, and rewards go to claims backed by a randomly sampled set of independent peers who stake tokens and lose them if an audit finds collusion. Splitting one identity into a hundred does not multiply influence: the attacker must recruit or control distinct stakers, fund their stakes, and risk slashing for every false endorsement. A yarrow-market dispute on a terrace can expose an echo of copied claims, but the costly, accountable endorsements are what limit sybil power.
